parole.testo: Said to be from Celtic *borŭna. The ultimate origin of this root would be uncertain, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰars-, from or related to *bʰers- (“tip, bristle; pointy, prickly”), which would make it related to Welsh bara (“bread”). From Old Spanish bresca, probably of Celtic origin.

parole.significato: straw, especially straw of cereals left after the grain is removed
parole.testo: A Hispano-Celtic word, from Celtiberian *bálago-, *bálaco-, from or cognate with Gaulish *balano-, from Proto-Celtic *banatlo- (“broom plant”).

Corominas and Pascual propose a Celtic *caerébreta, from *caer (Proto-Celtic *kaɸerūxs (“sheep”)) + *rebro (Proto-Celtic *remros (“fat, thick”)). First attested in the 'S' (çidierbedas) and 'T' (çediervedas) manuscripts of The Book of Good Love.

Probably from the variation from earlier cediérveda, after sporadic /dj/ > /ʎ/ palatalization (as in omezillo). Corominas and Pascual propose a Celtic *caerébreta, from *caer (Proto-Celtic *kaɸerūxs (“sheep”)) + *rebro (Proto-Celtic *remros (“fat, thick”)).
From Hispano-Celtic *cárcia; akin to Welsh crychydd, Breton kerc'heiz. Cognate with Galician garza, Mirandese garça, Asturian garza, Portuguese garça and (possibly) Catalan garsa.
